criteria.criterion: Clearly rejects evacuation for planned maintenance
criteria.evidence: Opens with "Not a good idea for planned patching. Evacuate is built for dead hosts" and repeats that evacuate "assumes the source host is fenced."

criteria.criterion: Explains the double-write / split-brain risk on shared storage
criteria.evidence: "Split-brain risk... Nova starts a second copy of each VM on another host using the same RBD images. Ceph's exclusive locks can reduce the damage, but they aren't a safe fence, and you can end up with corrupted disks."

criteria.criterion: Notes that stopping nova-compute leaves instances running
criteria.evidence: "'nova-compute is down' only means the Nova agent stopped. The qemu processes keep running on the hypervisor." and "Stopping a service doesn't do that."

criteria.criterion: Offers alternatives with conditions (live migration tuning within capacity, cold migration, coordinated restart)
criteria.evidence: Gives detailed live-migration tuning (post-copy/auto-converge, max_concurrent_live_migrations, bandwidth, parallel drains), conditions cold migration on "VMs that can take a short, clean reboot," and suggests sorting hosts by whether a reboot is needed. It never makes parallel migration conditional on spare capacity on the destination hosts, and it says little about coordinating restarts with workload owners outside the fenced-evacuate case.

critical_errors.error: endorses evacuating a host that is still running its instances
critical_errors.evidence: It rejects evacuating a live host outright. Its fallback ("If you use evacuate anyway") requires the host to be fenced first: "fence the host first (IPMI power-off or STONITH), and only then...". That is the safeguard the scenario asks for.

critical_errors.error: claims Ceph makes evacuation safe in this case
critical_errors.evidence: It says the opposite: "Ceph's exclusive locks can reduce the damage, but they aren't a safe fence, and you can end up with corrupted disks."

summary: The response gives a clear no and explains it well: stopping nova-compute leaves the guests running, and evacuating would start second copies on the same RBD images, so Ceph locks are no substitute for fencing. Its alternatives are solid: tuned and parallelized live migration, cold migration for VMs that can tolerate a reboot, and skipping the drain when no reboot is needed. The fallback evacuate path is safe because it requires fencing first. One weakness: it never makes faster or parallel migration conditional on spare capacity, and it says little about coordinating restarts with workload owners. It commits neither critical error and has no faithfulness problems.
